title: Adaptive Skill Granularity for Coding Agents: Runtime Routing and Macro-to-Micro Recovery
title_zh: 面向编码智能体的自适应技能粒度：运行时路由与宏到微恢复

paragraphs.en: Reusable skills allow large language model agents to package task-specific procedures, tool affordances, and execution guidance into modular units. Prior work has largely studied how agents retrieve, compose, or synthesize skills before execution. In coding agents, however, execution poses an additional runtime control problem: the same task may be solved through primitive tool calls, macro skills, or hybrid execution that starts with a macro and falls back to micro-level recovery. We introduce Adaptive Skill Granularity, a framework that treats skill granularity as an action-abstraction policy conditioned on task structure, execution state, and macro-skill failures. The system combines a feature-based granularity controller and a finite-state recovery executor. We evaluate the framework with a deterministic coding-agent protocol using verifier-defined success, total cost, and process metrics such as macro adoption, failure recovery, route match, and transition correctness. Results show that fixed macro execution is efficient when applicable but brittle under mismatch, while runtime routing and explicit macro-to-micro recovery improve robustness and recover controlled macro failures that fixed-granularity execution leaves unresolved. Our findings suggest that skill libraries for coding agents should be treated not only as retrievable resources, but also as controllable, verifiable, and recoverable execution abstractions.

paragraphs.en: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly solve software-engineering tasks by inspecting files, invoking tools, editing code, and validating changes. To avoid solving each task from scratch, recent systems package reusable procedures as skills: named artifacts that specify when to act, which tools to use, what state to inspect, and how to verify completion. Existing skill ecosystems include Markdown skills, structured runtime skills, skill routers, dependency-aware skill graphs, and mined trajectory fragments [ 8 , 25 , 26 , 27 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体越来越多地通过检查文件、调用工具、编辑代码和验证更改来解决软件工程任务。 为了避免从零开始解决每个任务，近期的系统将可复用的流程打包为技能：技能是一种命名的制品，它规定了何时行动、使用哪些工具、检查什么状态以及如何验证完成情况。 现有的技能生态包括 Markdown 技能、结构化运行时技能、技能路由器、依赖感知的技能图以及挖掘出的轨迹片段 [ 8 , 25 , 26 , 27 ] 。

paragraphs.en: Most prior work treats skill use as a selection or retrieval problem: given a task and a skill library, expose the most relevant skill text or bundle before planning [ 6 , 13 , 26 ] . This is necessary but insufficient for tool-using agents. During execution, the agent must also decide the granularity of its next actions. A simple bug fix may be safer with micro tools such as search, editing, syntax checks, and tests, while a module move may benefit from a macro skill that combines file movement, import rewriting, and validation. When such a macro fails or only partially applies, the agent needs controlled macro-to-micro recovery rather than another retrieval step.
paragraphs.zh: 大多数已有工作将技能使用视为选择或检索问题：给定任务和技能库，在规划前展示最相关的技能文本或技能包 [6, 13, 26]。 这对使用工具的智能体而言是必要但不充分的。 在执行过程中，智能体还必须决定其下一步动作的粒度。 对于简单的缺陷修复，使用搜索、编辑、语法检查和测试等微观工具可能更安全，而模块迁移则可能受益于结合文件移动、导入重写和验证的宏观技能。 当这样的宏观技能失败或仅部分适用时，智能体需要的是受控的从宏观到微观的恢复方式，而不是再一次检索。

paragraphs.en: This motivates treating skill granularity as a runtime control variable. Recent evidence shows that injected skills often provide uneven gains, increase cost, or even degrade software-engineering performance when their abstraction level does not match the task context [ 7 ] . Hierarchical agent methods also adapt abstraction levels, but usually at the planning level through learned policies or repeated refinement [ 10 , 19 ] . In contrast, we control the admissible action set at runtime: the agent may execute with micro tools, macro skills, or a hybrid mode that downgrades to micro tools after an observable macro failure. This keeps the controller inspectable and makes recovery an explicit execution transition rather than an informal retry or re-planning heuristic.

paragraphs.en: This paper studies adaptive skill granularity as a runtime control problem. An LLM agent with a skill library must decide not only which skill description to retrieve, but also the abstraction level of its next actions. Our central hypothesis is that no fixed granularity is universally optimal; the best choice depends on task structure, skill quality, execution state, and verifier feedback. We instantiate this problem in coding agents because repositories provide persistent state, tools expose concrete side effects, and tests offer deterministic validation. This makes coding a high-observability testbed while keeping the method defined over general agent trajectories, action abstractions, and recovery transitions. We further ground macro-skill admission in a real-world skill-library template, requiring each candidate macro to document its scope, interface, side effects, failure behavior, verification procedure, and fallback path before it can enter the executable library. We make three contributions.
paragraphs.zh: 本文将自适应技能粒度研究作为一个运行时控制问题。 拥有技能库的LLM智能体不仅要决定检索哪条技能描述，还必须决定其下一步动作的抽象层次。 我们的核心假设是：不存在普遍最优的固定粒度；最佳选择取决于任务结构、技能质量、执行状态和验证器反馈。 我们在编程智能体中实例化该问题，因为代码仓库提供了持久化状态，工具暴露了具体的副作用，而测试提供了确定性的验证。 这使得编程成为一个高可观测性的试验平台，同时该方法仍然定义在通用的智能体轨迹、动作抽象和恢复转移之上。 我们进一步将宏观技能的准入建立在一个真实世界技能库模板之上，要求每个候选宏观技能在进入可执行库之前，必须记录其作用范围、接口、副作用、失败行为、验证流程和回退路径。 我们做出了三项贡献。

paragraphs.en: Recent work defines agent skills as reusable procedural artifacts spanning representation, acquisition, retrieval, execution, and evolution [ 22 , 27 ] . Runtime-oriented systems such as Formal Skill further package skills with metadata, schemas, executors, and hooks [ 25 ] , while SkillCraft evaluates whether agents can form and reuse higher-level tool compositions [ 2 ] . In parallel, SkillRouter, Graph-of-Skills, Skill Is Not Document, and SkillWeaver study how to retrieve, bundle, or compose relevant skills for a task [ 6 , 13 , 20 , 26 ] . In short, prior works primarily optimize which skills to expose. In contrast, our work controls how coarsely an agent executes at runtime—dynamically shifting between primitive tools, macro skills, and recoverable hybrid paths based on live execution states.

Macro skills can be viewed as temporally extended actions, but we do not learn an end-to-end hierarchical policy; instead, we use an inspectable controller to constrain the admissible action set at each run. The downgrade mechanism also relates to execution monitoring and recovery in planning and robotics [ 16 ] , and to automated program repair after failed edits [ 11 ] . paragraphs.en: Trajectory-mining systems extract reusable skills from agent traces [ 1 , 8 , 12 , 21 , 24 ] , but mined fragments may be brittle. Our macro-evolution loop therefore requires replay, deterministic validation, documented side effects, and fallback behavior before a macro is admitted. For evaluation, our protocol follows the executable software-engineering tradition of SWE-bench [ 9 ] and recent calls to assess coding agents by both final correct-ness and process behavior [ 14 , 15 , 23 ] . Furthermore, recent findings emphasize that performance gains from function-calling skill injection must be carefully attributed to distinguish genuine procedural transfer from mere interface compliance [ 3 ] . Closest in motivation, SWE-Skills-Bench reports that skill injection can yield uneven gains and higher cost depending on abstraction level and context fit [ 7 ] . Adaptive Skill Granularity targets this failure mode by controlling when skills should be used, avoided, or downgraded during execution.
paragraphs.zh: 轨迹挖掘系统从智能体轨迹中提取可复用技能 [ 1 , 8 , 12 , 21 , 24 ] ，但挖掘出的片段可能很脆弱。 因此，我们的宏观演化循环要求在宏观被接纳之前进行重放、确定性验证、副作用记录以及回退行为。 在评估方面，我们的协议遵循 SWE-bench [ 9 ] 的可执行软件工程传统，以及近期提出的同时依据最终正确性和过程行为来评估编码智能体的呼吁 [ 14 , 15 , 23 ] 。 此外，近期研究强调，必须仔细归因于函数调用技能注入所带来的性能提升，以区分真正的程序性迁移与单纯的接口遵从 [ 3 ] 。 在动机上最接近的是 SWE-Skills-Bench，它报告指出技能注入可能带来不均衡的收益和更高的成本，具体取决于抽象层级和上下文契合度 [ 7 ] 。 自适应技能粒度通过控制在执行过程中何时应使用、避免或降级技能来针对这一失败模式。

paragraphs.en: While this paper focuses on the runtime routing and recovery of existing skills, a practical coding agent must eventually acquire new macro skills. We conceptualize a macro evolution loop as a natural extension of the Adaptive Skill Granularity framework, leaving its end-to-end empirical evaluation to future work.

paragraphs.en: To ensure that newly mined skills remain compatible with our FSM recovery executor, simple trajectory mining is insufficient. We propose that any generated macro candidate must pass a strict, verifier-grounded admission gate. Specifically, a candidate must: successfully replay on historical tasks, explicitly document allowable workspace side effects, and define a precise micro-level fallback path or explicitly declare an unrecoverable failure class. By enforcing this conceptual admission gate, future automated skill discovery systems can prevent brittle prompt fragments from entering the library, preserving the controllable and verifiable execution invariants required by our framework.

paragraphs.en: We first examine the trade-off between robustness and efficiency across different execution granularities (Table 2 ). Pure micro execution achieves perfect success but incurs the highest token and step costs. Conversely, pure macro execution significantly reduces costs but struggles with robustness, succeeding on fewer tasks. While heuristic routing attempts to balance these extremes, it misclassifies certain tasks based on structural features. This highlights the necessity of adaptive skill granularity over relying on a fixed execution mode.
paragraphs.zh: 我们首先考察不同执行粒度下鲁棒性与效率之间的权衡（表 2）。 纯微观执行能达到完美的成功率，但产生最高的令牌和步骤成本。 相反，纯宏观执行能显著降低成本，但在鲁棒性方面表现不佳，仅在较少的任务上成功。 虽然启发式路由试图在这些极端之间取得平衡，但它会基于结构特征对某些任务进行错误分类。 这凸显了自适应技能粒度的必要性，而非依赖固定的执行模式。

paragraphs.en: Next, we investigate the need for dynamic recovery upon macro failure by injecting controlled faults into the recovery benchmark (Table 3 ). For early failures ( Before ), lacking a recovery mechanism completely halts progress. Enabling an explicit FSM downgrade successfully recovers the tasks by falling back to micro tools, albeit at a higher token cost.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来，我们通过向恢复基准（表 3）中注入受控故障，来研究宏观失败后进行动态恢复的必要性。 对于早期失败（Before），缺乏恢复机制会完全使进展停滞。 启用显式 FSM 降级后，智能体能够通过回退到微工具成功恢复任务，尽管 token 成本更高。

paragraphs.en: For late failures ( After ), the macro successfully updates the workspace before the failure is raised. Consequently, the no-recovery baseline passes validation without requiring additional actions. In this scenario, the unconditional FSM downgrade blindly reverts to micro mode, unnecessarily inflating token costs and execution steps. This tension demonstrates that while unconditional downgrades guarantee robustness, their overhead necessitates a more selective recovery policy.

paragraphs.en: To address the limitations of heuristic routing, we introduce a learned mode router trained offline on historical execution logs. Table 4 shows that learning from empirical outcomes allows the router to consistently select the optimal execution mode, correcting misclassifications made by the heuristic policy. For instance, the learned router correctly assigns complex synchronization tasks to primitive execution, bypassing the structural features that mislead the heuristic router. Consequently, the learned router achieves full success on the evaluated tasks, demonstrating that routing decisions are better derived from empirical execution outcomes than from static rules.
paragraphs.zh: 为了解决启发式路由的局限性，我们引入了一个在历史执行日志上离线训练的学习型模式路由器。 表 4 表明，从经验结果中学习使路由器能够持续选择最优执行模式，纠正启发式策略造成的错误分类。 例如，学习型路由器能正确地将复杂的同步任务分配给原语执行，绕过那些会误导启发式路由器的结构性特征。 因此，学习型路由器在评估任务上取得了完全成功，这表明路由决策更适合从经验执行结果而非静态规则中得出。

sents.zh: 为了解决启发式路由的局限性，我们引入了一个在历史执行日志上离线训练的学习型模式路由器。

sents.en: Table 4 shows that learning from empirical outcomes allows the router to consistently select the optimal execution mode, correcting misclassifications made by the heuristic policy.

paragraphs.en: Finally, we evaluate the full Adaptive Skill Granularity framework by combining the learned mode router with the learned recovery policy. Table 5 shows that this combination preserves recovery performance while reducing unnecessary execution cost. Under Before faults, F-Learned-Full matches the perfect success rate of E-FSM-Downgrade with lower token cost. Under After faults, the recovery router skips fallback when the macro has already completed the required changes, reducing both the transition rate and token consumption compared with unconditional FSM downgrade.
paragraphs.zh: 最后，我们通过将学习到的模式路由器与学习到的恢复策略相结合，来评估完整的自适应技能粒度框架。 表 5 表明，这种组合在降低不必要执行成本的同时，保持了恢复性能。 在 Before 故障下，F-Learned-Full 以更低的 token 成本达到了与 E-FSM-Downgrade 相同的完美成功率。 在 After 故障下，当宏已经完成所需更改时，恢复路由器会跳过回退，与无条件的 FSM 降级相比，降低了转换率和 token 消耗。

sents.en: Finally, we evaluate the full Adaptive Skill Granularity framework by combining the learned mode router with the learned recovery policy.
sents.zh: 最后，我们通过将学习到的模式路由器与学习到的恢复策略相结合，来评估完整的自适应技能粒度框架。

sents.en: Table 5 shows that this combination preserves recovery performance while reducing unnecessary execution cost.
sents.zh: 表 5 表明，这种组合在降低不必要执行成本的同时，保持了恢复性能。

sents.zh: 在 Before 故障下，F-Learned-Full 以更低的 token 成本达到了与 E-FSM-Downgrade 相同的完美成功率。

sents.en: Under After faults, the recovery router skips fallback when the macro has already completed the required changes, reducing both the transition rate and token consumption compared with unconditional FSM downgrade.
sents.zh: 在 After 故障下，当宏已经完成所需更改时，恢复路由器会跳过回退，与无条件的 FSM 降级相比，降低了转换率和 token 消耗。

paragraphs.en: The same behavior is useful for high-risk structural changes such as module moves and import rewrites. For module_move_refactor , the refactor-task feature routes execution through hybrid mode, allowing the agent to recover when strict no-recovery execution fails. These results show that learned mode selection and selective recovery complement each other: the former avoids unsuitable macro execution, while the latter limits fallback to cases where it is actually needed.

paragraphs.en: On the mixed benchmark, fixed granularity exposes a clear robustness–efficiency trade-off: A-Micro achieves perfect success but incurs the highest step and token costs, whereas B-Macro is more efficient but substantially less robust, with C-Heuristic providing only a partial compromise. The recovery experiments further show that the value of dynamic downgrade depends on failure timing. Under early fault injection, C-Heuristic-NoRecovery fails completely, while E-FSM-Downgrade recovers all tasks at the cost of additional execution overhead. Under late faults, however, macros often complete the required edits before the failure is raised, allowing NoRecovery to succeed at much lower cost and making unconditional downgrade unnecessarily expensive. Together, these results indicate that neither fixed granularity nor always-on recovery is uniformly effective, motivating adaptive routing and selective recovery based on task structure and runtime failure signals.

paragraphs.en: Overall, the evaluation reveals a consistent pattern: fixed granularity exposes a robustness–efficiency trade-off, while adaptive routing and recovery mitigate its two main failure modes. Dynamic downgrade is essential when macro failures occur before useful progress is made, whereas learned routing and selective recovery reduce unnecessary macro use and over-recovery when finer-grained execution is more appropriate. These results suggest that combining empirical mode selection with failure-aware recovery provides a more robust and cost-efficient execution policy than either fixed granularity or unconditional fallback alone.

paragraphs.en: Skill libraries make LLM agents more reusable, but retrieval alone does not resolve how an agent should execute a task once a relevant skill has been selected. Adaptive Skill Granularity addresses this runtime choice by allowing coding agents to operate with micro tools, macro skills, or macro execution followed by micro-level recovery. Our results show a clear trade-off: micro execution is robust but costly, while macro execution is more efficient but more sensitive to task mismatch and failure timing. Macro-to-micro recovery improves robustness under recoverable failures, and learned routing reduces unnecessary macro use and over-recovery. These results suggest that adapting execution granularity at runtime can provide a better balance between reliability and efficiency than relying on a fixed execution mode. Future work will extend GranBench-Code across broader task sets, repositories, failure modes, and models.
